video_title: ESPN Front Office Insider on How Lakers Roster Can Compete with Thunder and Spurs - Sedano & Kap

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs and Thunder's draft capital makes Western Conference scary
quotes.excerpt: Cap space doesn't mean anything when your best free agents are on your own roster here.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean, I think first, I think after watching these two teams last night, I think it's a pretty scary thought for the rest of the Western Conference. I really do. And these teams are only going to get better when you look at, I have an article coming out tomorrow, these two teams got 50 draft picks in the next eight years coming their way. Think about that. They're only going to add to their roster here. I think from the Lakers' perspective, I think when you, we've talked about this before, we can talk about cap space until we're blue in the face. Cap space doesn't mean anything when your best free agents are on your own roster here. And best free agents in the league are on your own roster.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' cap flexibility with LeBron and Austin Reaves contracts
quotes.excerpt: If you have LeBron at $30 million and you have Reaves in the mid-$30 million, it still gives you flexibility.
quotes.quote: Austin Reaves' number really is not of consequence because he's basically going to stay on as a cap hold and then basically you're going to fill out your roster before you resign him here. But I think if you had, listen, if you had LeBron at around $30 million, and this is basing it off running this group back. This isn't basing it that we're going to be a team that's going to act as cap space. So if you have LeBron at $30 million and you have Reaves in north in the mid-$30 million here, it still gives you the flexibility to bring back Rui Hachimura if you want and also use your $15 million non-taxpayer level exception and have the flexibility in trades and everything like that.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers cannot compete with OKC or San Antonio by running back current roster
quotes.excerpt: It's hard for me to believe they can compete with either team. I really don't.

text_blocks.speaker: Kappy
text_blocks.text: Would you, could you look at bringing back the core of the Lakers? I'm talking about obviously Luka Doncic, he's signed, but LeBron, Austin Reaves, Marcus Smart, Rui Hachimura. Could you look at the core and say, you know what, we can build enough around them to beat Oklahoma City or San Antonio? Could you in your own mind?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: No, I don't think I don't think. Listen, to be honest with you, I don't think what they do if they bring back the same roster and if they go out in free agency, it's hard for me to believe they can compete with either team. I really don't. I mean, listen, you'd have to basically, things would have to line up perfectly. And why those teams are different, there's such an infrastructure there. There's an infrastructure of players on rookie contracts when you look at what Oklahoma City has been able to do and what San Antonio. Carter Bryant would be the starting small forward for the Lakers or power forward. He would be a starter. He's your seventh, eighth man in San Antonio. So I think it's, I don't think there's a one-year plan that you can put a roster together and think that next season you're going to be able to compete with either team. Now, you don't want to wave the white flag either here, but I think the plan would be that you probably want to mirror what Dallas did with Luka Doncic as far as adding some of the pieces that they did with a rim protector or a lob threat, a big wing, some shooting, which I think you already have on your roster here. But this is going to be a multi-phase process here. You're not going to be able to do everything you probably want just in one summer.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers won't be a 53-win team without LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: If you're willing to be content with that and go post-LeBron, you probably won't be a 53-win team.

text_blocks.speaker: Kappy
text_blocks.text: I guess I would just go back and ask this question if again, you're now, I'm asking you to play, you're in the Lakers organization. And you have to make a decision. Do we want to bring LeBron back because he's good for business and he's still a great player? Or are we thinking about the future and how to build a roster that can go 10, 12 deep like these teams that we're watching last night? Which direction would you go? And by the way, is LeBron the key to that? Maybe I'm looking at it all wrong.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Well, listen, I mean, like, so let's say you don't bring him back. Are you better next year? No. I don't think so either. So if you're willing to be content with that and basically kind of rip the band-aid off, right, and go post-LeBron, then you have to be content that you're probably not, you're going to be a much different roster, but you probably won't be a 53-win team. That's the reality of it with Luka and Reaves back, and then you kind of fill in the gaps as far as, you certainly want to go get a center, and then you want to fill in some other things here, whether it be in free agency or maybe some of your own players here. I don't think I don't think you can make the argument that you're a better team. You'll add a pick in the draft, which is the 20th to 25th pick, maybe you can move that for something else here. But yeah, it's, it's, as I've always said, with some of these teams that get older, and I know Lakers are a little bit different because they have Luka and Austin, when you don't have the infrastructure of younger players and you've traded those picks, and rightfully so, they've made deals that they to win, and you don't really have much to move in a deal in the future, it's tough. It's very difficult to build your roster in free agency. I'd rather, if you were the Lakers, I would rather have the group under contract not as a cap space team this summer.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers need to find developmental talent like OKC to build around Luka
quotes.excerpt: You have to go out and find the Julian Champagnies, the Luke Kornets in free agency.

text_blocks.speaker: George
text_blocks.text: Yeah, I mean, listen, the Lakers have not extended a first-round pick since 2005. That was Andrew Bynum. They did extend one second-rounder in Max Christie a few years ago, but then obviously had to trade him for Luka. They have done it in the pre-Rob, there was, I think they did a really nice job of finding young players, but none of those young players became the star that can lead you, right? They have one of those guys now in Luka, but they don't have the guys on those rookie contracts to your point, which creates a real problem, right? Like you have to hit on developmental pieces through the draft or whether you find them in the G-League, because here's the thing, you look at, you look at OKC, yeah, they traded for Caruso, but they had him in their program before, right? Like, you know what I mean? Like they had him on OKC's G-League team prior, so they knew what they had there. Lu Dort, they developed through the G-League. They've, they've found guys not just in the draft or early in the draft. Jalen Williams, I told the story to the audience last hour. They found him because they were scouting Chet Holmgren and realized, who the hell is this kid who's just playing full throttle even though his team's getting throttled in these games against Gonzaga and Santa Clara. They've just done, AJ Mitchell, right? They were scouting someone else, they found him.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: That's what you have to do, George. You have to go out and find the Julian Champagnies, the Luke Kornets in free agency. I know they paid part of the non-tax for him. Isaiah Joe, Kenrich Williams, Aaron Wiggins type players. That's what you have to go out and do. It's not about putting a $30 million offer sheet per year on Peyton Watson. That doesn't solve it here. But that's, the Mitchell one is a great example, he goes in the mid-30s here. But those are the type of guys as far as to build kind of a build around around Luka. And then, maybe there's an opportunity for you down the road to add another player to that group.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Robert Williams is the top free agent center for Lakers to target
quotes.excerpt: The one name that was basically picked up the most buzz, a lot of teams in Chicago last week, was Robert Williams.

text_blocks.speaker: Kappy
text_blocks.text: Bobby, let me ask you, because you mentioned a center, and George and I went back and forth all year long about DeAndre Ayton. I mean, to me, you get what you pay for. And you got an $8 million center who played like an $8 million center. Except, except he shouldn't play, his the bigger issue I have with him, Bobby, is that he should not be an $8 million center, and he's only an $8 million center because of his own fault, is what is the way I view it. Right, so we argued about this all season long, but in the final analysis, I mean, that's what he was paid, and he played in almost every game, and some games he was on the floor, but he didn't really show up. So the question really is, are there big men out there that the Lakers might be able to acquire this offseason that can just be competitive with the likes of Chet Holmgren or Wemby? Now, Wemby's a freak, I get it, he's a once-in-a-lifetime sort of talent. But is there anybody out there that the Lakers could sign and go, at least now you've got a competitive big man out there?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: The one name that was basically picked up the most buzz, a lot of teams in Chicago last week, was Robert Williams. That's the name. And now you have to be cautious with that because your, the games availability, the minutes, you have to, that's the one guy, I don't want to say neutralized Victor Wembanyama, but I think guarded him probably one of the best this certainly in the playoffs in the first round. That would be, that would be the guy. You've got, he's probably one of the top unrestricted free agent centers out there. And I think he gives you that shot blocker, that rim protector, that guy that can, you know, lob threat for for Luka. Now the question is, the cost, what's the cost? Is it $12, $13 million? I think that's kind of where his, where his range is, but there'll be other teams that also see that. There's teams out there, certainly Atlanta and Boston and Clippers are teams that have money to spend and everything like that. But that would be, that would be the one guy if I could circle in free agency on, on kind of your, on your wish list, that would be the guy.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo to Lakers is difficult due to trade assets and fit
quotes.excerpt: The only way that he could ever get to Los Angeles would basically play hardball.

text_blocks.speaker: George
text_blocks.text: Giannis. So the Lakers obviously called about him, I guess at the deadline. Shams is reporting they will likely be at least inquiring about him. First things first, I don't think he's a great fit with Luka. Second of all, you'd have to trade Reaves, which again, reportedly Luka does not want to get rid of Reaves. What do you view the Giannis situation to be in regards to the Lakers and then at large, how do you view the Giannis situation?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Well, with Reaves, he would even have to agree to it. And I don't even know, how does he fit with Milwaukee if you're paying him significant money? So that's the hard part there as far as piecing, you could basically trade for him and take him in with cap space if you want to and still retain Reaves here. But it's hard because what else would you have to send from the Lakers besides the 25th pick in the draft and a first in 2031 and 2033 and some pick swaps. I don't know if that does it for Milwaukee. I think the only way that he could potentially would ever get to Los Angeles would basically play hardball and basically say this is the only team I'll sign an extension with, which would be the Lakers here. I don't know if the Bucks would call his bluff on that. So yeah, it's a hard situation to point down as far as him getting to Los Angeles just based on the lack of resources to trade for him. And then fit-wise, you would basically have him and Luka, and you could maybe still have Reaves on your roster, then you'd be filling in the gaps with guys on probably on minimum contracts.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami and Minnesota are top trade destinations for Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: Miami probably already has a built-in package when you look at the 13th pick in the draft and two future first.
quotes.quote: I would say Miami. I think they've probably already have a built-in package when you look at the 13th pick in the draft and then they've got two future first in 2031 and 2033 also. You have Tyler Herro, who's on an expiring. He'll be on an expiring. Nikola Jovic, Jaime Jaquez Jr., you could probably put in some salary filler there. I think that's probably one. I think Minnesota will be interesting. Certainly they're a team that circled the wagons with him around the trade deadline. It will cost them, and it will cost them probably Jaden McDaniels and a combination of Rudy Gobert, Karl-Anthony Towns, or Naz Reid with that. So you're looking at probably two players, at least two players out of your starters or reserves that are going to be going out. And another question is what's left. They only have one first to trade.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James will consider options, market dictates contract value
quotes.excerpt: The market tells you that he's not going to Brooklyn and he's not going to Chicago in cap space.

text_blocks.speaker: Kappy
text_blocks.text: Bobby, I just want to bring it home then for a quick second about LeBron. I've always thought that LeBron, he's never going anywhere. This is the first offseason that I think that it's conceivable that he could maybe decide to go somewhere else. Do you think it's a foregone conclusion that LeBron is automatic back to the Lakers?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Oh, no. Yeah, no, I don't. I mean, I think he'll, I think he'll look at, I think it's, I think certainly from him being in the LA area for a long time here and he's got their roots there certainly with his wife and daughter and his sons that are Arizona and Bronny on their roster. I think there's a, I think there's a comfort level certainly being on, on this, on this roster coming back. I do think as far as what makes sense for him, the hard part is that, I see all these, some of these shows and they say, well, why should LeBron take a discount as far as a contract? Well, the market tells you that, right? Like the market tells you that he's not going to Brooklyn and he's not going to Chicago in cap space here. And everybody else is basically got the $15 million non-tax and veteran minimum here. So when you're looking at Cleveland at the minimum, and you're looking at Denver at the minimum, or you're looking at Golden State, maybe a little bit more than that, those are your other options as far as what he could be, what he could be looking at.
